title: From dry to sweet
subtitle: Reading a Chenin label
objectives: Name the sweetness terms on Loire labels
Explain how botrytis affects sweet Chenin

steps.title: Sweetness terms
steps.body: Loire Chenin labels may say sec, dry; demi-sec, off-dry; moelleux, sweet; or doux, very sweet. Vouvray and Montlouis can be any of these, depending on the vintage: in warm years with botrytis, more sweet wine; in cool years, more dry and sparkling. If no term appears, check the back label or producer.

steps.title: Botrytis
steps.body: In Anjou's Layon valley, autumn mists bring noble rot. Coteaux du Layon, and its top crus Bonnezeaux and Quarts de Chaume, make sweet wines from botrytised Chenin. Quarts de Chaume became the Loire's first Grand Cru in 2011. Chenin's acidity keeps them fresh, and they can age for 50 years or more.
steps.highlight: Quarts de Chaume: first Loire Grand Cru

steps.prompt: Order these Loire terms from driest to sweetest.
steps.explanation: Sec is dry; doux is the sweetest.

steps.title: Sparkling
steps.body: Chenin's high acidity makes excellent sparkling wine. Vouvray and Montlouis make pétillant and mousseux; Saumur Brut and Crémant de Loire use Chenin with Chardonnay and Cabernet Franc. They're made by the traditional method, with honeyed, apple flavours.

steps.prompt: Which Loire appellation became the first Grand Cru in 2011?
steps.explanation: Quarts de Chaume makes sweet, botrytised Chenin.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Sec, demi-sec, moelleux and doux mark sweetness
Coteaux du Layon and Quarts de Chaume are sweet botrytis wines
Chenin's acidity makes fine sparkling wine
